reasons: F01, F02, F03: material weakness in internal control specifically over revenue, with an adverse auditor ICFR opinion, so revenue recognition controls are known to be ineffective.
F07: the filing contains a restatement of prior periods, which shows errors have already been found and raises the chance that more remain.

F08, F09: revenue is mostly recognised over time and contract assets/unbilled amounts are significant, so revenue depends heavily on management estimates that the weak controls (F02) may not check properly.
R08, R19: accruals are high and positive, and operating cash flow and net income have opposite signs, so reported earnings are not backed by cash.
R17, R13: the Dechow F-score is above its threshold, and soft assets are more than 75% of total assets, which leaves a lot of room for estimates and discretion.
F19, F21, R16: covenant breach, waiver or amendment, plus a capital raise and securities issued, create pressure to present strong results to lenders and investors.
F22, R05: a major acquisition in the year adds complexity (purchase accounting, integration) and depreciation is slowing, a possible earnings lever.
Mitigating: no going concern (F04), no auditor change (F05), no SEC inquiry or class action (F16, F17), no CEO/CFO turnover (F14, F15), leverage stable (R07) and no non-GAAP emphasis (F26).
